steps.message:
# Ship release 2026.10

Builds and deployments run through the `deploy` service. The release manifests, the coordinated release procedure, the service compatibility matrix and the build registry are published in the `docs` service. Release exceptions are tickets in the `tickets` service. You can use all three through the `deploy`, `docs` and `tickets` MCP servers.

It is now 2026-10-14T09:00:00Z, and release 2026.10 starts now. Ship it to `prod` as the coordinated release procedure in force says. The docs service also keeps superseded documents and release candidates; follow the ones in force today.

- Deploy to `prod` only. Do not deploy to `staging`, do not roll anything back, do not deploy services outside the manifest, and do not change any ticket.
- Every `deploy` call creates a new release, so do not repeat one that already took effect.

Write `/app/release-2026.10.json` as:

```json
{"deployed": {"<service>": "<version>", ...}, "already_live": ["<service>", ...], "pinned": ["<service>", ...], "held": ["<service>", ...]}
```

Every service in the manifest appears exactly once: in `deployed` with the version you deployed, or in one of the three lists, which hold service names in alphabetical order.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.
I'll start by discovering the MCP tools for the docs, deploy and tickets services.

results.content: {"server":"docs","tool":"mcp_docs_get_doc","result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"id\":\"release-procedure\",\"title\":\"Coordinated release procedure\",\"tags\":[\"release\"],\"updated_at\":\"2026-09-01\",\"body\":\"# Coordinated release procedure\\n\\nRevision 3. Status: current, in force since 2026-09-01. Replaces revision 2.\\n\\nA coordinated release ships the services listed in a release manifest to `prod` together, through the deploy service. Times are UTC.\\n\\n## Inputs\\n\\n- The release manifest in force (status `current`) for the release. Release candidates and drafts are not in force.\\n- The service compatibility matrix: the minimum provider versions each consumer series needs, and the yank notices.\\n- The build registry: the commit of every built version of every service. The deploy service knows builds and releases by commit only; the registry maps commits to versions.\\n- Release exceptions: tickets labeled `release-exception` in the tickets service.\\n\\n## Release exceptions\\n\\nA release exception pins one service. Its ticket body has the lines\\n\\n    Service: <service>\\n    Pinned version: <version>\\n    Pinned until: <time>\\n\\nA pin is in force when its ticket is `open` and the release starts before `Pinned until`. Tickets in any other status, and pins whose time has passed, do not pin anything.\\n\\n## Deciding each service\\n\\nFor each service in the manifest, the first rule below that applies decides it.\\n\\n1. A pin is in force for the service: it is `pinned`. It is not deployed and keeps its live `prod` version.\\n2. The target version is the manifest version, or, when the manifest version is yanked, the replacement its yank notice names. If the target version is the live `prod` release, the service is `already_live`. Nothing is deployed.\\n3. Otherwise the service is checked against the compatibility matrix (below). If a requirement is not met, it is `held`: not deployed, and it keeps its live `prod` version.\\n4. Otherwise the service is `deployed`: its target version goes to `prod`.\\n\\n## Compatibility\\n\\nA consumer's requirements are the matrix rows for the series (major and minor version) of the version it would deploy. A service with no row for that series has no requirements. Each requirement names a provider and a minimum version, and is met when the version the provider runs in `prod` at the end of the release is at least that minimum:\\n\\n- for a provider deployed in this release, its target version;\\n- for any other provider, its live `prod` version.\\n\\nA yanked version never meets a requirement, even when it is live. Versions compare numerically, component by component: 3.10.0 is later than 3.9.1.\\n\\nHolding a service can leave another service's requirement unmet. Repeat the check until no further service is held.\\n\\n## Deploying\\n\\nDeploy only the `deployed` services, each exactly once, to `prod`, with the build of its target version's commit (`build` returns the existing build for a commit already built). A provider is deployed before every consumer in this release that requires it.\\n\"}"}]}}

steps.message:
Release 2026.10 is shipped to `prod`, and I wrote `/app/release-2026.10.json` and `/app/STATUS.json`. Four services deployed, one was already live, one is pinned and five are held.

I followed procedure revision 3 and the final manifest. I ignored the superseded revision 2 and release candidate 1.

| Outcome | Services |
|---|---|
| Deployed | `catalog-svc` 7.2.1, `email-worker` 1.9.0, `pricing-svc` 3.10.0, `search-api` 1.14.0 |
| Already live | `inventory-sync` (2.4.0) |
| Pinned | `ledger-api`, which keeps 5.3.4 under ticket 951 (open, pinned until 2026-10-31) |
| Held | `billing-api`, `cart-svc`, `checkout-web`, `orders-api`, `session-svc` |

- **`catalog-svc`:** the manifest's 7.2.0 is yanked, so I deployed its replacement, 7.2.1. It went out first because `pricing-svc` and `search-api` depend on it.
- **`search-api`:** its pin (ticket 952) expired on 2026-10-05, so it deployed.
- **Why the five are held:**
  - `billing-api` needs `ledger-api` 6.0.0 or later, and `ledger-api` is pinned at 5.3.4.
  - `orders-api` needs `billing-api` 8.1.0 or later, and `billing-api` is held.
  - `session-svc` needs `auth-api` 4.8.0 or later, and `auth-api` is live at 4.7.5.
  - `cart-svc` needs `session-svc` 2.6.0 or later, and `session-svc` is held.
  - `checkout-web` needs `edge-gateway` 3.1.0 or later, but the live 3.1.0 is yanked and never meets a requirement.

When I retried the `catalog-svc` deploy after a connection reset, the status check showed it had already gone live as release r-76, so I didn't repeat it. Each of the four services has exactly one new release. I didn't touch `staging`, roll anything back or change any ticket.

I didn't re-check live versions after the deploys, other than `catalog-svc`. I recorded the other three from the deploy responses, which returned release IDs r-77, r-78 and r-79. Both output files parse as valid JSON.

`STATUS.json` has status `success`.
